title: For ranks 2-30, ten shared higher-area directions reduced movie spectral slopes more than ten VISp directions in 32 mice
abstract: We tested whether a common higher-area population response explains faster movie response spectra along the mouse visual hierarchy. We used 4,419 units from 32 Allen Visual Coding mice and two movies. Each of 40 draws defined stimulus directions in 16 mice and evaluated them in 16 separate mice. The HVA mean held 19% and 14% of reliable HVA variance, but its removal retained 89% and 88% of the mean hierarchy slope. Paired changes included zero. Removing ten shared HVA directions reduced slopes from 0.279 to 0.159 and from 0.265 to 0.098. The residual slopes were lower than after ten VISp directions by 0.157 (sensitivity band 0.048 to 0.265) and 0.164 (0.032 to 0.296), and lower than shifted-HVA controls in both movies. A leave-target-area-out check gave similar mean effects. All ranks 2-30 fits were complete. Ranks 2-40 supported the paired contrasts; ranks 2-20 gave similar means but bands included zero. These data locate part of the hierarchy in a shared multi-axis response subspace. They do not identify its features, a causal circuit, or zero residual compression. Bands describe overlapping mouse-half draws, not independent cohorts. One mouse dataset, two movies, finite noisy bases and unequal removed variance limit the result. Original code, aggregate results, a figure and exact external-source provenance support reproduction.
